one_line_contribution: An intervention-based test of whether the counterfactual value of a retrieved agent-memory exemplar, after subtracting the type-level procedure a fixed static prompt already delivers, is a property of the item or of the reader that consumes it — operationalized as the disattenuated cross-reader rank agreement of per-item leave-one-out residuals over four readers plus a cross-fitted transfer-of-selection deployment test.
closest_prior_work: ExpGraph 2605.30712 (VERIFIED via s2cli paper: 2026-05-29, 'Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory', abstract explicitly claims 'experience reuse across diverse tasks and executor models', ablated at module level on aggregate success). It asserts exactly the invariance this proposal wants to falsify, but only at system/aggregate level, so it motivates rather than pre-empts — a reviewer will nonetheless ask why the experiment is not simply ExpGraph's own executor swap instrumented with per-item removals, which would make the result about a published system instead of an in-house ALFWorld bank. Two verified home-literature threats the proposal never cites and that dent its 'nobody has asked' framing: LLM-R 2307.07164 (VERIFIED, EACL, 88 cit) and EPR 2112.08633 (VERIFIED, NAACL, 987 cit) both learn example-utility scores under one scoring LM and evaluate them under other LMs — aggregate accuracy, not per-item counterfactual rank agreement, so the decomposition and the disattenuated-rho estimand remain new, but 'does example utility learned under one consumer work for another consumer' is an old question in in-context learning, not a question this proposal opens. CUE-R 2604.05467 (VERIFIED, 2026-04-07) is the per-item intervention method under a single generator; CHIME 2609.02074 (VERIFIED, 2026-09-02) and ReMe 2512.10696 (VERIFIED, ACL, 55 cit — its headline is precisely a cross-model memory-scaling claim, Qwen3-8B+memory > memoryless Qwen3-14B) are aggregate. The Compliance Trap 2607.10608 (VERIFIED via the recent search) already reports reader-strength dependence of memory harm and finds conflicting memory 'disproportionately harms stronger agents' — the opposite sign to P3's prediction that long-detour items cost the weaker reader more; the proposal cites it in the brief but does not reconcile P3 with it, and a reviewer who knows that paper will read P3 as a coin flip already called the other way. Could not verify: 2509.12765 (DIG confidence gain) — s2cli returned 'not found on S2 or HF'; the proposal leans on it for the 'does not examine transfer across generators' claim, so that leg of the novelty argument is unverified.
strongest_objection: The headline P2 is more likely to be unmeasurable than to be answered, and if it is measurable it is confounded. (a) Power: a per-item residual at S=6 rests on ~12 paired Bernoulli contrasts, so its standard error is roughly sqrt(2*0.25/12)*100 ≈ ±14 net, and each split half (~6 contrasts) carries ±20. For split-half rho_AA >= 0.5 the true between-item SD of static3-net residuals would have to be about 20 net points — while the entire aggregate k3 − static3 is +17.2 spread over three positions, i.e. roughly +6 per item on average. The realistic landing zone is rho_AA, rho_BB ≈ 0.2–0.4, which the proposal's own risk section concedes degrades the paper to class-level results, and the 0.3–0.5 dead zone is exactly where neither the premise nor the falsifier of P2 fires (the automated entailment check flags the same window, and calls P5 outright unresolvable at S=4). A paper whose headline number has a decent chance of being 'reliability too low to say' is a reject in discussion. (b) Validity: cross-reader agreement of removal effects is confounded with success base rates. An item retrieved mostly for games where B is on the floor (or A near ceiling) has a near-zero residual under that reader for reasons that have nothing to do with reader-specific item value, so rho_AB is pushed below 0.5 even in a world where item value is literally identical in latent terms; the paired design controls the game, not the reader's operating point on the difficulty curve. Nothing in the plan separates this scale artifact from genuine consumer-specificity, so the headline 'residual does not transfer' has a mundane alternative explanation the paper cannot exclude. (c) The evidence for the title's decomposition and the evidence for 'where the residual lives' are different quantities: C4/C5 are with-arms on the natural k=3 set with no static3 present, so P3 measures gross class value, not the static3-net residual the title claims to localize.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Turn reliability into a pre-registered gate rather than a hope: run a cheap pilot (~30 items, S=10, one reader) and report rho_AA before committing the 85k-episode budget; publish the per-item claim only if rho_AA >= 0.5, otherwise declare the manufactured-class study the paper up front and reallocate episodes from E2 to E3/E4. 2) Add a base-rate null that calibrates the estimator: construct a reader whose item values are identical by construction but whose success rate differs — A with a reduced step budget, quantized weights, or a higher temperature — and show the pipeline returns a disattenuated rho near 1 there. Without this, no value of rho_AB below 0.5 is interpretable. Reporting residuals on a logit/latent scale, or restricting to games where both readers are off floor and ceiling, would blunt the same confound. 3) Measure C4/C5 with static3 present so P3 is about the residual, not about gross class value, and report the class contrast on the same footing as the decomposition. 4) Run C's and D's static3+REMOVE arms at S>=6–10 with a pre-registered minimum rho_CC/rho_DD, or drop P5 rather than report an unresolvable arm. 5) Fix P4's redundancy (only two of the three thresholds are independent) and add an item-property predictor as a real floor.
missing_baseline: A same-weights, capability-shifted reader — A run with a reduced step/decoding budget, quantized, or at higher temperature — which moves success rate while holding reader identity fixed. The stated factorial has A vs B (family-matched, capability differs), A vs D (capability-matched, family differs) and A vs C (same backbone, policy shifted), but no cell in which only the operating point moves, and that is the cell that both separates 'capability gap' from 'reader identity' in the headline A-vs-B contrast and calibrates the base-rate artifact described above. Secondary omission: E4's floors are random-3 and similarity top-3; a reviewer will also demand a cheap item-property scorer (length, type match, trajectory quality heuristic) as the baseline that a reader-specific value estimate must beat, since beating similarity alone does not show that anything reader-specific was learned.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My queries, all answered by channel (a), the s2cli literature command (s2=ok hf=ok on every run); WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so no section text was read. (1) mechanism: 'counterfactual value of retrieved in-context example transfers across different reader models' — nothing relevant (nearest returns were counterfactual-prompting baselines 2605.01048 and counterfactual-task benchmarks 2307.02477). (2) mechanism, --recent: 'per-item memory utility re-measured under a different consumer model agent experience bank transfer' — returned MemHarness 2607.28272, Compliance Trap 2607.10608, MEMPROBE 2606.24595, StreamMemBench 2606.14571, LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493; none re-measures the same items' counterfactual value under two consumers, though 2607.10608 already establishes reader-strength dependence of memory harm with the opposite sign to P3. (3) closest named method: 'ExpGraph model-agnostic experience learning graph memory executor models utility-aware ranking' — 2605.30712 plus SE-GoS 2609.08228, EXG 2605.17721, HAGE 2605.09942, all aggregate. (4) home literature: 'in-context demonstration selection does not transfer across language models example value is model-specific' and (5) 'learning to retrieve prompts in-context learning scoring LM transferability of retriever to other language models' — these surfaced EPR 2112.08633 and LLM-R 2307.07164, the cross-consumer example-utility question in its in-context home, which the proposal's own check missed entirely. IDs verified with s2cli paper: 2605.30712 ok, 2609.02074 ok, 2604.05467 ok, 2507.04480 ok, 2512.10696 ok, 2512.24503 ok, 2504.11393 ok, 2307.07164 ok, 2112.08633 ok; 2509.12765 NOT FOUND on S2 or HF and is therefore unverified — the proposal relies on it for 'DIG explicitly does not examine transfer across generators'. Judging the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above the median — it names its channel, reports per-query returns with ids, verified CHIME's id, and correctly identifies ExpGraph as the nearest named method — but it is narrow in vocabulary. It searched agent memory and training-data valuation and never searched in-context example selection, where the transfer-across-consumers question has been asked since 2021; the Related Work sentence 'no per-item score has been re-measured under a second consumer' survives only in its narrow per-item-counterfactual reading, and the Abstract's broader framing does not. It also verified only one of the eight ids its novelty argument rests on, and one of the unverified ones (2509.12765) does not resolve.
